Basim Al Zabir Shammo Information & Communication Engineer · Robotics and Machine Learning Researcher Biography My background is in Information and Communication Engineering at Pabna University of Science and Technology. I work on robotics and machine learning, bringing together sensor data, hardware, and computer models. My research focuses on digital twins, sensor fusion, and robots that use cameras to understand their surroundings. My projects include mobile robots, Arduino systems, and small hardware prototypes. I also study health monitoring with PPG signals and computer vision for satellite images and traffic analysis. Research Interests Areas of focus Physics-informed machine learning Digital twins Sensor fusion Autonomous robotics Computer vision Biomedical signal processing

title: Physics-informed digital twins
text: ← All projects Hardware-in-the-loop · Sensor fusion Physics-informed digital twins I built a digital model of a small motor system. The model uses sensor readings from the real hardware. It tracks changes in load and heat during use. This helps study the system and predict how hot it may become. Hardware setup for sensor fusion and embedded-system experiments.

title: Vision-based mobile robotics
text: ← All projects Computer vision · Coverage planning Vision-based mobile robotics I worked on a mobile robot that uses a camera to find cracks. The robot follows a zig-zag path to cover the area. Camera data and infrared sensors help it avoid getting stuck. It covered 94.17% of the test area in a Webots simulation. Mobile robotic platform with sensors and embedded electronics.

title: 17-DOF humanoid robot
text: ← All projects Robotics · Hardware assembly 17-DOF humanoid robot I worked with a humanoid robot with 17 degrees of freedom. Its joints use servo motors to move. The frame holds the motors, wires, and control parts. This work involved the robot’s hardware and joint setup. 17-DOF humanoid robot in the laboratory. Basim with the humanoid platform.

title: Voice and Radio Controlled Robot
text: ← All projects Arduino · HC-05 Bluetooth · Android app Voice and Radio Controlled Robot We built this robot using Arduino and an HC-05 Bluetooth module. We also made an Android app to send voice commands. The app sent these commands to the robot over Bluetooth. The robot moved in response to those commands. Voice and radio controlled robot built with Arduino and an HC-05 Bluetooth module.

title: First Arduino Obstacle-Avoiding Robot
text: ← All projects Arduino · Sonar sensor First Arduino Obstacle-Avoiding Robot This was our first robot built with Arduino and a sonar sensor. The sensor checked for objects in front of the robot. When it found an object, the robot stopped. The project focused on sensing obstacles and controlling movement. First Arduino robot with a sonar sensor, programmed to stop when an obstacle is detected.

title: Mini Obstacle-Avoiding Robot
text: ← All projects Custom JRC board · Sonar sensor Mini Obstacle-Avoiding Robot We built this mini robot with a custom JRC board. It used a sonar sensor to check the path ahead. When it found an object, it changed its path. This allowed the robot to move around obstacles. Mini obstacle-avoiding robot with a custom JRC board and sonar sensor.

title: Knock-Pattern Door Unlocking Mechanism
text: ← All projects Arduino · Knock sensing · Door lock Knock-Pattern Door Unlocking Mechanism We built a door lock that responds to a set knock pattern. A buzzer worked as the sensor and picked up the knocks. The Arduino checked the pattern against the stored one. When the pattern matched, the door unlocked. Arduino door-unlocking prototype using a buzzer to sense a knock pattern.

title: Physics-Informed Digital Twins for Micro-Mechatronic Systems
text: This study looks at how a digital model can track a small motor system. It combines a maths-based model with readings from several sensors. The data helps track the system and predict changes in heat. We also studied how certain the model’s predictions were.

title: Vision-Based Crack Detection and Coverage Planning
text: This study combines crack detection with route planning for a mobile robot. A camera model finds cracks while the robot follows a zig-zag path. Infrared and camera readings help the robot avoid getting stuck. The method reached 94.17% coverage in a Webots simulation.

title: Vision Transformer-Based Damage Assessment
text: We used satellite images to study building damage after Hurricane Harvey. A model called ViT-B/32 reached 97.85% accuracy in our tests. It performed better than the CNN model used for comparison. Heatmaps showed which parts of each image influenced the result.

title: Machine Learning-Based Hepatitis C Detection
text: We compared ten machine learning models for detecting Hepatitis C. The models used clinical data to make their predictions. AdaBoost gave the highest accuracy among the models we tested. The study explored how these tools could support automated detection.

title: Smartphone-Based Physiological Monitoring
text: This study used a phone camera to record changes in blood flow. We processed these PPG signals with machine learning models. The models estimated blood pressure, blood oxygen, stress, and heart health risks. The aim was to study health monitoring with a mobile device.

title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Nightmares in Children
text: We studied how machine learning could help predict nightmares in children. The work brought data analysis into child mental health research. It focused on using data to support psychological assessment. The study was presented at COMPAS 2025.

title: Stress Detection Using PPG Signals
text: We studied how PPG signals could help detect stress. Machine learning models looked for patterns in these signals. The aim was to assess stress using data from the body. The research was presented at QPAIN 2025.

title: YOLOv8-Based Vehicle Detection and Classification
text: We used YOLOv8 to find and classify vehicles in traffic footage. The study focused on roads in Bangladesh. It explored how real-time video could support traffic monitoring. We presented the work at ICRPSET 2024 in Rajshahi.

title: Real-Time RFID Authentication and Access Control
text: ← All projects Embedded systems · RFID · Networked logging Real-Time RFID Authentication and Access Control We built a door access system using an RFID reader and an ESP8266 board. It checked the tag before allowing entry. A servo controlled the lock, and a buzzer gave a sound signal. The system saved the tag ID and access result in a local database. RFID access-control hardware prototype. System diagram: RFID authentication, lock control, and networked logging.
